messages.content: Let’s settle the Chicago flights for the same Friday-to-Monday weekend. There are two of us, with the concert Saturday and the museum Sunday still fixed. I want to understand what we gain by paying more for better times.

I found four workable combinations. The Friday midday nonstop leaves Denver at 12:05 p.m. and reaches Midway at 3:25 p.m.; the less expensive nonstop leaves at 7:10 p.m. and reaches O’Hare at 10:38 p.m. Monday, you can leave O’Hare at 8:15 a.m. or Midway at 3:20 p.m. All prices below are totals for two adults.
Give me the combinations, including what the different airports mean for reaching the hotels we were comparing.

Midday Friday plus early Monday is $706. Midday Friday plus 3:20 Monday is $782. Late Friday plus early Monday is $548, and late Friday plus 3:20 Monday is $624. From Midway, allow roughly 35–50 minutes to either downtown hotel; from O’Hare, about 45–70 minutes depending on traffic. The hotels are close enough together that the transfer difference between them is minor.
So the cheapest choice would put us at the hotel close to midnight Friday and take away Monday morning too.

Yes. After landing at 10:38 p.m., a realistic hotel arrival is 11:45 p.m. to 12:15 a.m. For the 8:15 a.m. Monday flight, you would need to leave the hotel around 5:45 a.m. That combination saves $234 compared with taking both more convenient flights, but it compresses both ends of the weekend.
The midday flight Friday seems clearly better for the concert weekend. How much usable time does the later return really add? Checkout will probably be at noon.

It adds most of Monday morning and lunch. You could check out at noon, leave both bags with the hotel, have lunch nearby, return for them around 12:40 p.m., and leave for Midway by 12:50. That should put you at the airport around 1:35 p.m. for the 3:20 departure. The early flight would mean no Monday activity at all.
And the incremental cost from the midday-out, early-back combination is $76 total, correct?

Correct. The outbound stays the same, and moving the return from 8:15 a.m. to 3:20 p.m. raises the total from $706 to $782 for both travelers. It also uses Midway in both directions, which keeps the ground plan consistent.
That is worth it. Select the Friday 12:05 nonstop to Midway and the Monday 3:20 nonstop from Midway for both of us.

Selected pending payment: Friday Denver–Midway nonstop, 12:05–3:25 p.m., and Monday Midway–Denver nonstop at 3:20 p.m., for $782 total for two adults. Friday should leave time for an unhurried hotel arrival and dinner; Monday allows checkout, bag storage, and lunch downtown.

Can you choose seats now? For my seat, use a window if one can be selected. If this fare does not release seats until check-in, keep the itinerary and try for the window then rather than changing flights.

Advance seat selection is not available on this fare, so I have left the flights unchanged. I noted the window request for your seat and will apply it at the earliest check-in opportunity; your spouse’s seat remains unselected. Nothing has been charged yet.
